summary: Extend the existing arithmetic calculator's POST /calculate endpoint with a new pow operation (a ** b), reusing the existing request/response shape and error handling, without introducing any precondition for pow and without touching memory operations, other arithmetic operations, or routes.
goal: Callers can request exponentiation (pow) through POST /calculate the same way they already request add/sub/mul/div/mod, with pow computing a ** b and never rejected by a precondition check the way div/mod are.
background: Follow-on to the done initial-calculator change. Today POST /calculate supports add, sub, mul, div, mod; there is no way to raise a to the power of b through the API, forcing client-side computation.

in_scope.text: Add pow to the op enum in openapi/openapi.yaml for POST /calculate, as an additive-only change.
Extend contracts/Calculator.ocl with a pow operation contract that computes a ** b and defines no precondition.
Add a new Gherkin Scenario for pow to requirements/calculator.feature.
Implement pow in src/calculator.ts: extend the Operation union, add Calculator.pow, and add the calculate() switch arm returning a ** b.
Add or extend contract tests in tests/contracts/*.test.ts covering pow, derived from the OCL/Gherkin for this change.

out_of_scope.text: Memory operations (src/memory.ts, contracts/Memory.ocl, requirements/memory.feature) are unchanged.
Existing operations add/sub/mul/div/mod keep their current behavior, contracts, and tests; no refactor of them.
No new HTTP routes; pow only extends the existing POST /calculate endpoint.

No precondition or domain-error check is introduced for pow (e.g. must not reject b <= 0, a == 0, or negative base with fractional exponent) — pow does not get the div/mod zero-divisor PreconditionError pattern.
Overflow / special-value behavior for pow (Infinity, NaN, 0 ** 0) beyond native JS ** semantics is deferred, not tightened, in this change.
No change to the POST /calculate response JSON shape; pow reuses the existing result shape.

assumptions: The existing PreconditionError type and the div/mod zero-divisor pattern established in initial-calculator remain unchanged; pow simply never throws it.
pow reuses the existing calculate() response shape (no new response fields); exact shape is confirmed at OpenAPI apply time, consistent with the other operations.
Native JS ** operator (IEEE-754 double) semantics for edge cases (very large exponents, 0 ** 0, NaN-producing inputs) are acceptable for this change unless a future change tightens them.
constraints: pow must not have a zero-divisor-style precondition: OCL, tests, and implementation must not reject b <= 0, a == 0, or similar inputs for pow (Change Context §4 NFR1, §6).
The op enum change in openapi/openapi.yaml must be strictly additive: no existing enum value, route, or schema may be removed or narrowed (Change Context §4 NFR5).
contracts/Calculator.ocl remains the DbC source of truth for pow; contract tests are derived from OCL, not written ahead of it (Change Context §4 NFR6, repo adapter policy).
Stack stays as-is: TypeScript/Node, existing OpenAPI/OCL/Vitest toolchain (Change Context §5); no new dependencies for pow.

success_criteria.text: openapi/openapi.yaml op enum includes pow and passes Redocly lint (--extends=spec) with only an additive diff versus the pre-change spec.
contracts/Calculator.ocl documents a pow operation computing a ** b with no precondition clause.
requirements/calculator.feature contains a new Scenario for pow asserting a ** b results for representative inputs.
src/calculator.ts implements Calculator.pow and calculate() handles op: "pow", returning a ** b.
tests/contracts/*.test.ts includes passing tests asserting pow results for representative inputs and asserting pow never throws PreconditionError.
All pre-existing contract tests and Gherkin Scenarios for add/sub/mul/div/mod and memory operations continue to pass unmodified (no regression).

open_questions: Overflow / special-value behavior for pow (very large exponents, 0 ** 0, negative base with fractional exponent) is left to native JS ** semantics unless a later change tightens it — non-blocking, matches initial-calculator's deferred div/mod sign-convention precedent (Change Context §7).
Exact response JSON shape for pow results is deferred to OpenAPI apply, expected to match existing operations with no new shape — non-blocking (Change Context §7).

human_gate.reason: Scope, precondition exclusion, and stack are already settled by the user's instruction and Change Context (gate required: false, confidence: high, no blocking §7 items); this Brief only makes that delta concrete, it does not introduce a new material default, breaking change, money/authz boundary, or low-confidence judgment.
